segments.text: so sometimes you might have a cloud
watch alarm that you've set up that you
don't want to set off but you need to
test to make sure that the actions that
you have tied to that cloudwatch alarm
actually work
so there's a nice little command that we
can use to do this manually for testing
purposes without actually having to set
this off so for instance here in my
cloudwatch dashboard I have a S3 size
alarm so this goes off when a particular
bucket gets to a very large size now I
don't want to actually show up that
bucket with the amount of files that I
need to trigger that alarm
so what I can do instead is go over to
my AWS command line tool and I can
control Cloud watch from there
it's the AWS command line tool has a set
alarm state
command
and it's going to take an alarm name
a state value
and we'll set this to alarm to actually
set off the alarm
and then we need to give it a state
reason
all right and then we can run this
command
and then we'll see that our
Cloud watch alarm enters the alarm State
here for us and we can watch any actions
or other things that we have hooked up
to this alarm
now the alarm will return to the OK
State after the next scheduled check of
that cloudwatch alarm
